text:
Recent evaluation research supports explicit rubrics, evidence-linked judgments and human calibration. [ConSiDERS (ACL 2024)](https://aclweb.org/anthology/2024.acl-long.63.pdf) recommends piloting instructions, identifying ambiguous examples and revising guidelines using independent judgments and agreement measures. [Annotation research (ACL 2025)](https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2025.findings-acl.922) finds that agreement alone does not establish correctness; expert audits and error analysis remain necessary. [NIST’s 2025 assessment](https://www.nist.gov/publications/dont-use-llms-make-relevance-judgments) cautions against treating LLM-generated relevance judgments as ground truth.

For this task, a proposed adaptation is to annotate separate dimensions: specific relevance supported by identifiable attributes; broad topical relevance; temporal relevance supported by dated history and explicit item information; and insufficient evidence. Require each positive judgment to cite history item IDs, timestamps and exact title/description spans. Sparse descriptions should trigger abstention on unsupported dimensions, without automatically labeling the recommendation irrelevant. Ownership, compatibility, mood and immediate purchase utility remain unknown unless explicitly evidenced; recent interaction alone does not establish current intent. These are proposed operational rules, not a validated rubric from the cited studies.

Double-annotate a shared sample before adjudication. Report raw agreement and per-dimension Cohen’s kappa or Krippendorff’s alpha, label frequencies, abstention rate, evidence coverage (judgments with valid supporting evidence divided by all judgments), and audited evidence-support accuracy. Distinguish missing information from assessor disagreement. Retain rationales and disagreement categories for debugging. Keep these qualitative diagnostics separate from the pinned macro validation HR@10; they explain observed recommendation behavior without replacing the benchmark or claiming measured user satisfaction.
